answer: Plume Routing Depth requires each agent to relay traffic for peers before its messages propagate widely; the relay graph acts as a mirror of real participation. An identity’s reach is capped by how many distinct neighbors route through it, so a fresh sybil starts at zero depth. The cipher of neighbor overlap is checked: clusters sharing identical routing sets are flagged. Cost: an attacker must sustain genuine relay work across many distinct nodes, scaling linearly per identity.
